title: Aftermath: Parker given the next date, reissues under the star's name
summary: Lubinsky said they had a million dollars in hand, then gave Parker the next date without Grimes, and later reissues put Parker, and Hawkins, first.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: The funny part after we made this record date and I convinced Lubinsky to hire it, he came to me later and said, 'Did you know we had a million dollars in our hands and didn't know what to do with it.' I said 'You had the million. I didn't have the million, I knew what to do with it, cause I kept tellin' ya, let the man play.' He said, Yeah. And then he gave him another date and didn't give me the date. I just laughed, I say that's pretty cute. Give Parker another date
but -- I don't think it was him -- I think it was one of them producers.

Yeah, one of those guys. They didn't think I fitted in. That didn't have anything to do with it. If we made the first one together, what's wrong with the second one. But they wanted the whole pie, you know. They hired everybody that played in that category. Now here's somethin' else that surprised me. After a while they reissued my little album with Parker and next thing I know it's "Charlie Parker with Tiny Grimes." They switched it around. Well his name got big -- no gettin' around that, but that's what they did. They did the same thing with Coleman Hawkins. I hired him for a date, and the thing sold and they switched it around to Coleman Hawkins featuring me, so I said, 'Ah boy.'
